paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: Illustrating the empirical generalization errors and sharpness measures with respect to QLoRA weights. (<ref>) Smaller adapters with a rank of 16 achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima. (<ref>) An ensemble of k adapters leads to lower generalization errors and Hessian traces. Here, we fix the sum of the dimensions of k adapters to be equal to 256. (<ref>) QLoRA, which is trained on a quantized base model, yields lower generalization errors and Hessian trace values compared to LoRA.
model_annotation: This grouped bar chart, titled "Error (RTE)," illustrates the generalization error on the RTE task for two methods—LoRA and QLoRA—across different rank values. The horizontal axis is labeled "Rank" and contains four categories: 4, 16, 64, and 256, arranged in ascending order from left to right. The vertical axis represents error values on a linear scale, ranging from approximately 0.3 to beyond 0.9, with tick marks at 0.3, 0.6, and 0.9. Each rank category contains two bars side by side: a blue bar representing LoRA and a green bar representing QLoRA. All bars include error bars (black vertical lines with caps) indicating variability. At rank 4, the LoRA bar reaches approximately 0.59 and the QLoRA bar approximately 0.51. At rank 16, LoRA is approximately 0.61 and QLoRA approximately 0.45. At rank 64, LoRA is approximately 0.68 and QLoRA approximately 0.50. At rank 256, LoRA is approximately 0.75 and QLoRA approximately 0.63. Across all rank values, the green QLoRA bars are shorter than the blue LoRA bars. A legend is positioned in the upper-left area of the chart, displaying a blue square labeled "LoRA" and a green square labeled "QLoRA." The bars are not sorted independently but follow the ascending order of the rank categories.
